doc.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024

title: Who young students cite as masters today
summary: Incoming Michigan students still name Coltrane, Parker and Rollins, plus younger players; the 1960s-80s generation seems neglected.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Who are the great masters for 20-year-olds now? I mean we moved from generation to generation. You know Coltrane was the zenith for many years. Who do they cite now as their influences?

You know I mean it’s very interesting and that’s another great question. I mean we do ask a lot of the young students coming in to audition for us who apply to Michigan, you know who are you checking out and who are you interested in and you know almost to a fault there’ll be Coltrane or Parker or Sonny Rollins are still on the list. I mean I think that those players are still incredibly important to them. But there will be you know Patrick Bartley and you know, other younger players, and sometimes there are players that you know we haven’t heard of because you know they’re not huge names but they are occupying a corner of the young player universe that we just haven’t accessed yet. But it’s an interesting mix of still the masters, which is great, or the people we think of as

the masters. But also a body of younger players. And you know I don’t notice players so much — like Michael Brecker’s name may come up but it seems like there’s maybe a generation of players that are not getting listened to as much and maybe so we sort of stop in the early ‘60s and then they sort of missed some of the ‘60s, ‘70s and ‘80s, and then it’s more into the 2000s. So this is the first time I’m really thinking about it this way so it’s a half-formed thought but it does seem like the early masters are there and then maybe there’s the Joe Hendersons or the, you know, the players who are a little bit younger and maybe not getting the attention that we might hope. And then there’s a bunch of younger players.
